paper_title: Scalable Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition using Random Kernel Approximation
paper_summary: The paper introduces a scalable variant of Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (EDMD) that constructs its feature dictionary via random approximations of a kernel function. Classic EDMD struggles with high‑dimensional state spaces because it requires many basis functions, leading to large computational burdens. The authors present two random feature generation strategies: data‑independent random Fourier features for translation‑invariant kernels, and the data‑dependent Nystrom method which works with any kernel. Both methods embed the system state into a lower‑dimensional random feature space, yielding a compact EDMD matrix that still approximates the Koopman operator accurately. An adaptive scheme is also proposed to add random Fourier features incrementally as needed. Numerical experiments on two benchmark dynamical systems demonstrate that both random‑feature approaches achieve competitive Koopman approximations with far fewer snapshots than standard Kernel‑EDMD. The work shows that random kernel approximations can bring EDMD to large data regimes while preserving its interpretability and modal structure. This contribution paves the way for applying data‑driven dynamical mode analysis to high‑dimensional problems in fields such as fluid dynamics and control.
relevance: By enabling EDMD to scale to large state dimensions and snapshot counts, the paper addresses a major bottleneck in Koopman‑based data analysis. It demonstrates that random kernel approximations can retain the accuracy of Koopman operator estimates while drastically reducing computational cost. The adaptive random‑feature strategy offers a new avenue for efficient model building in real‑time applications. Future work may explore kernel selection, sparsity promotion, and integration with control design for complex high‑dimensional systems.
